leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight round-1 configurations include optical lattice clocks, with the same two credited names, Katori and Ye, and with citations that differ only in wording. Five of the six (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce) have it as a stand-alone single-part prize. Danielsson includes it as one part of a two-part prize with B040. Four of the six moved to B015 from other opening first or higher placements (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce), so the apparent breadth reflects movement during round 1 as well as the opening rankings. The supporters share the view that the magic-wavelength lattice, inter-laboratory agreement at 10^-18 and demonstrated uses (millimetre-scale redshift, constants, dark matter) make this more than a better number. They differ in how much weight they give to the 2005 and 2012 precedents, to the unfinished redefinition of the second, and to the contributions of NIST, PTB, SYRTE and other groups outside the pair. Several name the lattice scheme and the 10^-18 regime as what the citation must say. Two members (Eriksson, Olsson) list B015 only as an alternative and do not prefer it.

Danielsson alone prefers a two-part prize pairing lattice clocks with IceCube, giving three laureates (Katori, Ye, Halzen). He values both as cases where nature supplied a clue and an instrument was built to read it, but concedes single-name credit for IceCube is the weak point. Pearce, who opened with B040 first, and Danielsson both name B040 as an alternative, not as a preferred part, and Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Johansson and Olsson each questioned a sole credit for a collaboration of this size, citing AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES. It is not shared whether source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are mature enough, or whether a defensible second or third name exists within the three-person limit.

Eriksson alone prefers topological insulators (Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan), citing a falsifiable theory, independent transport and ARPES confirmation, and no overlap with the 2016 prize. Mehlig lists B051 only as an alternative and Pearce ranked it seventh at opening. Eriksson himself concedes the credit is the weak point: Mele is omitted from his trio, the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal and the Fu-Kane and Moore-Balents work lie outside the credited names, and Mehlig's own trio of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp differs from Eriksson's. He says he would support B015 if the attribution cannot be resolved.

Olsson alone prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer), as a theory-plus-experiment door-opener with wide reproduction. Eriksson holds B017 as an alternative. Mehlig and Danielsson respond that the pairing mechanism is unresolved and that the platform may be early. Olsson accepts the maturity concern and the unresolved credit for Cao and the Dean, Young, Efetov and Yacoby groups, and says she would not oppose B015 if the committee prefers a metrology prize.

areas_of_agreement: B015 is the most widely held explicit preference: six of eight configurations include it, all with the same credited pair, Katori and Ye, and no member proposes a different pair.

Independent comparison between laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) at the 10^-18 level is cited as the maturity evidence for B015 by the supporters, and Eriksson also accepts it as real reproducibility.
Members who prefer B015 say the citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and the 10^-18 regime, and should not rest on the redefinition of the second, which has not happened.
Every member who is not currently preferring B015 (Eriksson, Olsson) still lists it as an alternative and says they would support or not oppose it if their own preferred credit cannot be resolved.

The single-name IceCube credit (B040) is widely regarded, including by its two former advocates Danielsson and Pearce, as hard to defend without expert input on the AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES history.
B012 (circuit QED) is not preferred by anyone. Johansson, Kroll, Eriksson, Lindroth and Olsson all raise the 2025 prize on circuits and the exclusion of Blais as obstacles for 2026.
Several members (Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson, Pearce, Kroll) say they rely on memory or on colleagues for credit details and would welcome expert reports.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a new principle (many-atom, Doppler- and recoil-free interrogation at the magic wavelength, argued by Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce and Johansson) or a large quantitative step on the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock work (Eriksson, Olsson, and the reservation most B015 supporters themselves record).

Whether a metrology achievement meets the statutory emphasis on discovery or invention, or whether a new phenomenon (B017, B051, B040) should be preferred. Johansson says B015 is weaker if the committee wants a new phenomenon.

Whether the diffuse neutrino flux and the source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) are firm enough to call B040 neutrino astronomy now. Pearce says the diffuse flux is firm and the sources are still developing, but Mehlig, Kroll and Olsson regard it as not yet ready.
Whether the mechanism of superconductivity and correlated states in magic-angle graphene must be settled before B017 is prized, and how much twist-angle disorder matters.
attribution_disputes: B015: whether Katori and Ye alone fairly represent the lattice clock, given Lemonde, Pfau, Lemke, Ludlow and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups, raised by Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce and Johansson. No member proposes an alternative pair.

B040: the credited list contains only Halzen. Danielsson, Pearce, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Johansson and Olsson note the collaboration scale and the AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES predecessors. Pearce argues Halzen's conception of the cubic-kilometre detector is unusually identifiable, and Olsson would want a clear historical record before supporting it.

B051: Eriksson's trio (Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan) omits Mele, while Mehlig's trio keeps Mele and omits Hasan. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (deceased) and Fu, Moore and Balents are outside the credited names.

B017: Yuan Cao and the early theory of Santos, Lopes dos Santos and Peres, and the Dean and Young groups, are outside the credited names, and the three-person limit restricts any two-part combination.
B012: a three-name configuration excludes Blais, the lead theory author, raised by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson.
maturity_disputes: B015: the redefinition of the second is pending. Pearce, Kroll, Johansson and Mehlig treat it as a timing question, not a bar. Lindroth, Kroll and Eriksson ask whether the committee should await it or rest on demonstrated 10^-18 performance.
B040: Pearce, Kroll and Mehlig say source identification is still moderate in significance and developing, so a citation to neutrino astronomy might be easier to defend later.
B017: Olsson, Eriksson and Mehlig agree that the unresolved pairing mechanism makes the platform possibly early, though Olsson thinks reproduction across many groups argues for recognition.
B051: Eriksson considers the field mature, with fifteen years of independent confirmation, and the main issue is credit, not maturity.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, works closely with superconducting-circuit groups at Chalmers, and says he would recuse or defer on B012 attribution. He also notes closeness to B011. His opening first choice B012 should be read in that light. He reports no tie to B015.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his PhD. He describes Jun Ye's JILA group as in the same Boulder precision-spectroscopy tradition, with no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye. This bears on B015 and he asks that the committee note it. He also sits in WACQT management, which touches B012 only indirectly.

Pearce (chair) works in the Fermi-LAT collaboration and in cosmic-ray, gamma-ray and X-ray instrumentation, so he has a field-level interest in B040 and B013 with no recorded tie to any credited name, and would declare this if either enters a final configuration.
Danielsson discloses an intellectual interest in cosmology (B028) from his work on de Sitter space and dark energy, and no institutional conflict.

Eriksson chaired the 2025 committee, which he notes is relevant to circuit QED overlap but not to recusal. Olsson and Johansson are both at Chalmers, noted as an institutional connection not tied to any candidate either proposes.
questions_for_round2: For B015, can the committee agree a citation wording that names the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and the 10^-18 regime, and that does not overlap the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock citations? Lindroth and Kroll are asked to draft it, and can the committee state in one sentence what is new relative to those prizes?

Do Lindroth, Kroll and an external reviewer consider that the contributions of Lemonde, Pfau, Lemke, Ludlow and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups are adequately recognised by naming only Katori and Ye, or does the credit need to change?
Should the unfinished redefinition of the second be counted as supporting evidence, treated as timing only, or omitted from the citation altogether, and does it argue for waiting a year?

Is B015 a discovery or invention in the statutory sense, and do Eriksson and Olsson now rank it as acceptable, given that both list it as an alternative? If not, what specific change in B051 or B017 would they need?

Can a defensible credit for B040 be established within three names or fewer, including whether AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES pioneers or detector co-builders should be named? If not, do Danielsson and Pearce drop B040 as a preferred part?

If B015 stands alone, does the committee want a second part at all, and which candidate would be both distinct from precision metrology and fit within the three-person limit? B015 plus any three-name entry would exceed it, and Danielsson's B015 plus B040 is the only such pairing so far.

For B051, can Eriksson and Mehlig resolve whether Mele can be separated from Kane, and how the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal and 3D theory would be acknowledged, before this is carried into the final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 has moved towards B015, with six of eight explicit preferences and an identical credited pair, but most of that convergence is new: four supporters changed from a different opening first choice, and every B015 supporter records the same novelty and lineage reservation against the 2005 and 2012 prizes. Eriksson and Olsson prefer B051 and B017 respectively and treat B015 only as an alternative. Round 2 should test whether the convergence survives scrutiny of the lineage argument and the omitted clock groups, and decide whether any second part is workable under the three-person limit. I take no position on the outcome.
